ideas.hook: Everyone's locking in till December 31st. I think we picked the wrong finish line.
ideas.script: Everyone's locking in till December 31st. I think we picked the wrong finish line. [pause] Since September there's this trend called the Great Lock In. People take the last four months of the year to fix themselves. Gym, sleep, money. Before January even hits. And honestly, I love it. I'm trying to do it too. [pause] But here's what I noticed. For us, January isn't the real reset. Ramadan is. And it's expected around early February, depending on the moon. That's like three and a half months away. [pause] Think about it. Every year we hit Ramadan cold. First week we're dying at suhoor, can't focus in taraweeh, and the phone's still running our life. So what if this lock-in is the warm-up? [pause] Right now I'm trying three things. [fill in: your real three, e.g. Fajr on time, less screen time, one page of Quran a day]. Small. Boring. But by February they won't be new anymore. [pause] So I'm not locking in for January. I'm locking in for Ramadan. What's the one thing you want locked in before Ramadan? Drop it below and I'll check on you.

sources.title: BuzzFeed: The Great Lock In is taking over TikTok again (Sep 2026)
The National: Expected Ramadan 2027 start date

ideas.title: Lock in for Ramadan, not January
ideas.why: Rides the Great Lock In / winter arc trend (Sept–Dec 2026) and gives it a Muslim twist: Ramadan is expected around early Feb 2027, about 3.5 months away.

ideas.hook: There's a discipline habit that takes three days a month, and almost none of us do it.
ideas.script: There's a discipline habit that takes three days a month, and almost none of us do it. [pause] In Islam there's something called the white days. The 13th, 14th and 15th of every Islamic month. A lot of people fast them. And there's a hadith in Sahih Bukhari where Abu Hurairah said his close friend, the Prophet ﷺ, advised him to do three things: fast three days every month, pray two rak'ahs of Duha, and pray witr before sleeping. [pause] Three days. Not thirty. Three. [pause] And here's why I think it hits different for guys our age. We talk about discipline all day. Cold showers, 5am routines. But fasting is the original discipline training. You tell your body no, for Allah, when nobody's watching. [pause] This month's white days are basically right now, and the next ones land around late November. Check your local masjid's calendar. [fill in: be honest about whether you've done this before]. I'm going to try it next round. [pause] If you've never fasted outside Ramadan, try one day. Just one. Comment 'in' and let's do it together.

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1981 (fast three days each month, Duha, witr)

ideas.title: The 3-day-a-month discipline habit (white days)
ideas.why: It's 14 Jumada al-Awwal 1448 today (Oct 25), right in the white days, and the next ones fall around late November. It recasts fasting as the original discipline training, which fits the lock-in/discipline wave.

ideas.hook: If you're applying everywhere and nobody's calling back, you need to hear this.
ideas.script: If you're applying everywhere and nobody's calling back, you need to hear this. [pause] Statistics Canada just put out September's numbers. Canada lost 68,000 jobs. And people 15 to 24 took 48,000 of those. Ontario's unemployment is at 7 percent, the highest of the big provinces. So if you're a young guy in Ontario and it feels impossible right now? It's not all in your head. [pause] But here's the part I had to tell myself. A hard market explains it. It doesn't excuse me from trying. [pause] As Muslims we believe your rizq is already written. It's coming. But tawakkul isn't sitting on the couch. The Prophet ﷺ told a man, tie your camel, then trust Allah. That's in Tirmidhi. You do everything you can, and you leave the result to Him. [pause] So right now I'm [fill in: what you're really doing, e.g. handing resumes in person, asking people at the masjid, learning one skill]. And whatever you do, don't touch haram money because things are slow. The halal door might open slower, but that's the one with barakah. [pause] Comment where you're at. Still searching, or finally got something?

sources.title: The Hub: Canada shed 68,000 jobs in September (Oct 9, 2026)
Jami at-Tirmidhi 2517 ('Tie it and rely on Allah', graded hasan)

ideas.title: Can't find a job right now? It's not just you
ideas.why: StatCan's Sept numbers (Oct 9): youth lost 48K of Canada's 68K lost jobs, and Ontario sits at 7.0% unemployment. That's fresh local pain for his exact viewer, turned into tawakkul plus effort and staying away from haram shortcuts.

ideas.hook: This Sunday, your Fajr alarm is going to be wrong.
ideas.script: This Sunday, your Fajr alarm is going to be wrong. [pause] November 1st, clocks fall back an hour here in Ontario. Sounds like a gift, right? Extra hour of sleep. [pause] But here's what happens to a lot of us every year. Fajr suddenly shows up an hour earlier on the clock. Isha's earlier too. And if your alarm is still set for the old time, you wake up, the sun's already up, and Fajr's gone. [pause] [fill in: if it's true, 'and honestly, that's happened to me before. Not because I didn't care. Because I didn't plan.'] [pause] So here's what I'm doing this week. I'm grabbing my masjid's new timetable for November. I'm resetting every alarm. And I'm using that extra hour Saturday night to actually sleep earlier, not scroll later. [pause] Because a clock change is the perfect excuse. And excuses are exactly what we're trying to get rid of this year. [pause] Tag the brother who's definitely missing Fajr on Sunday.

sources.title: Time Out: When is the time change in Canada 2026 (falls back Nov 1)

ideas.title: This Sunday your Fajr alarm is wrong (clocks fall back)

ideas.hook: More than half of Canadian guys our age are on social media over three hours a day.
ideas.script: More than half of Canadian guys our age are on social media over three hours a day. And yeah, I see the irony of telling you this on TikTok. [pause] This is from a survey by the Canadian Men's Health Foundation. Two thousand Canadian men. Fifty-three percent of guys 19 to 44 said they're on social media more than three hours a day. And the heavy users were more than twice as likely to report anxiety. [pause] Three hours a day is twenty-one hours a week. That's a part-time job we're not getting paid for. [pause] But here's the part that got me. Henoc Muamba, the ex-CFL player, said the real damage is comparison. We're measuring our normal life against everyone else's highlight reel. [pause] And honestly, we already have the fix for that. The Prophet ﷺ said look at those below you, not those above you, so you don't look down on Allah's blessings on you. That's in Sahih Muslim. [pause] My screen time right now is [fill in: your real number]. I'm trying to get it under [fill in]. Comment yours. Honest numbers only.

sources.title: CP24/CTV: Former CFL player wants men to be more aware of how social media makes them feel (Oct 24, 2026)
Canadian Men's Health Foundation study release (Oct 7, 2026)
Sahih Muslim 2963 (look at those below you)

ideas.title: Half of guys our age are on social media 3+ hours a day

ideas.hook: The quarter-zip guys were onto something. But most of us copied the wrong part.
ideas.script: The quarter-zip guys were onto something. But most of us copied the wrong part. [pause] If you missed it, two friends from the Bronx posted a TikTok switching from 'Nike Tech guy' to 'quarter-zip guy.' Reportedly over thirty million views. And suddenly guys everywhere started dressing like they've got a job interview. [pause] And I get it. When you dress better, you carry yourself better. I've felt that. [pause] But here's what I keep thinking. You can change the fit in one day. The person inside it takes way longer. [pause] So if you're making the switch, make the real one too. From the guy who prays when it's convenient, to the guy who prays on time. From the guy who talks big, to the guy who keeps his word. From the guy scrolling at 2am, to the guy who sleeps so he can make Fajr. [pause] The Prophet ﷺ said Allah doesn't look at your appearance or your wealth. He looks at your hearts and your actions. That's in Sahih Muslim. [pause] So what's your switch? Finish it in the comments. From the guy who... to the guy who...

sources.title: KRDO/CNN: A new generation of men are dressing for success (Jan 2026)
Sahih Muslim 2564 (Allah looks at hearts and deeds)

ideas.title: The quarter-zip guys changed the wrong thing
ideas.why: It borrows the 'from X guy to Y guy' identity-switch line from the 30M-view quarter-zip TikTok and turns it inward to salah, character and sleep. It ends on a fill-in-the-blank CTA built to get comments.
